intent: Name what the card is about in a short headline.
typical_uses: The one-line headline at the top of a Card

dont_use_when.situation: The headline of a placeholder for a region with nothing to show
The title of a modal dialog
The title of a status message
The title of one row in a list of similar rows

invariants.text: Its default size follows the nearest Card's `size` (heading-2 at default, body at sm); `typography="panel"` sets the body size at the heading-2 weight with normal letter spacing whatever the Card's `size`.

Without `render` CardTitle is a div. With `render={<h3 />}` (any heading level) the element changes and the title class stays, with the UA heading margins and font reset at zero specificity, so the heading measures and paints as the div did.

anti_patterns.dont: Rely on CardTitle alone to give a card a place in the page's heading outline
anti_patterns.do_instead: Render it as a heading element with `render={<h3 />}`, which keeps the part's own styling; `role="heading"` with `aria-level` is the fallback where the element cannot change

render.states: render replaces the rendered div with an element the caller supplies
render.because: useRender's render prop takes an element or a function that receives the props to spread (CardTitle passes no state of its own), so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property. It is for the heading element, such as `render={<h3 />}`.

good.title: A headline rendered as a level-3 heading

bad.title: The explanation folded into the headline
bad.code:
<CardHeader>
  <CardTitle>Team plan. Billed monthly, 5 seats in use.</CardTitle>
</CardHeader>
bad.why: CardTitle is the headline; the supporting sentence belongs in CardDescription, which carries the muted body text and gets its own header row.

render.description: TS: ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, {}> | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. render replaces the rendered div with an element the caller supplies. useRender's render prop takes an element or a function that receives the props to spread (CardTitle passes no state of its own), so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property. It is for the heading element, such as `render={<h3 />}`.
